messages:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a big spike of OTLP exporter failures in staging right after we turned on per-tenant egress quotas. Exporter_queue_depth jumped and we started getting transient gRPC UNAVAILABLE errors.
Anika: Ugh. Saw that too. Looks like clients are piling up and the gRPC channel is getting overwhelmed. Any chance the pump/backoff config is still on the old defaults?
Jon: I pulled the exporter metrics: export_attempts_total increased, export_failures_retryable rose ~4x. queue_size was hitting limit and we had very little jitter on reconnects.
Lee: Could be a combo of per-tenant throttles + small retry budget causing aggressive reconnect storms. Do we have a per-exporter circuit breaker/window?
Olivia: Not today. We rely on a global async queue and gRPC reconnect defaults. We should add a soft throttle and an adaptive backpressure window per-tenant.
Sam: Proposal: add a small per-tenant in-memory buffer + token-bucket rate limiter and an adaptive drain window that increases backoff when gRPC errors spike. That would avoid hammering the downstream collector.
Anika: Sounds good. Also add HTTP fallback for exporters when gRPC is overloaded. But make it gradual — HTTP path must be stricter (smaller batch size, longer timeouts).
Jon: Example config I sketched (for the exporter operator):
```yaml
otlp_exporter:
  protocol: grpc
  timeout: 10s
  retry:
    max_attempts: 4
    backoff:
      base: 250ms
      max: 5s
      strategy: exponential
      jitter: 0.25
  queue:
    size: 3000
    per_tenant_shard: true
  throttle_window_ms: 1500
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    protocol: http
    http_batch_size: 128
    http_timeout: 20s
```
Lee: I like the per_tenant_shard flag. It prevents noisy neighbors from starving others. Also include a metrics exporter for per-tenant queue_depth and export_latency_p95 so we can alert before saturation.
Olivia: One other gotcha: when switching to HTTP fallback, we should preserve ordering for spans within traces. HTTP batches must include sequence metadata so the collector can re-order if necessary.
Sam: Good call. We'll add sequence_id + parent_span_hint in the payload.
Anika: Rollout plan: feature-flag the per-tenant buffer + throttle in staging for 48h, watch exporter_queue_depth and export_failures_retryable, then enable HTTP fallback behind a separate flag. Canary on 5% of tenants first.
Jon: Also, let's tune client-side connect_timeout lower (500ms) and keep grpc call timeout higher (10s) — that prevents slow connects from occupying worker threads.
Sam: Can infra-bot trigger a canary deploy for the exporter config on staging now?
infra-bot: Deploy queued: otlp-exporter-config-v2 -> staging (canary 5%). Started at 2026-03-18T15:22:00Z.
Lee: I'll add dashboards: per-tenant queue depth heatmap, export_failures by code, and a chart for backoff_window_size over time.
Olivia: If we see persistent HTTP fallback usage for a tenant, we should surface a billing/usage note to the console so customers know we're throttling.
Anika: Agreed. And add an alert: if >10% tenants are in fallback for >30m, page infra oncall.
Sam: Thanks all — follow-up PR from me with the operator change + smoke tests. Will link when ready. :thumbsup:
